as ''CSM (VSK) Miercurea Ciuc'' | ground = [[Stadionul Municipal (Miercurea Ciuc)|Municipal]] | capacity = 2,480 | owner = [[Miercurea Ciuc|Miercurea Ciuc Municipality]] | chairman = János Bokor | mgrtitle = Head coach | manager = [[Valentin Suciu]] | league = [[Liga I]] | season = [[2025–26 Liga I#Play-out round|2025–26]] | position = Liga I, 11th of 16 | website = {{URL|http://fkcsikszereda.ro/}} | current = 2026–27 FK Miercurea Ciuc season | kit_alt1 = | pattern_la1 = _blackshoulders | pattern_b1 = _ciuc1920h | pattern_ra1 = _blackshoulders | pattern_so1 = | leftarm1 = e62224 | body1 = | rightarm1 = e62224 | shorts1 = 000000 | socks1 = e62224 }} '''Asociația Futball Klub Csíkszereda Miercurea Ciuc''' ({{IPA|hu|ˈt͡ʃiːksɛrɛdɒ|lang}}, {{IPA|ro|ˈmjerkure̯a ˈtʃjuk|lang}}), commonly known as '''Csíkszereda Miercurea Ciuc''' or simply '''Csíkszereda''', is a Romanian professional [[Association football|football]] club based in [[Miercurea Ciuc]], [[Harghita County]], that competes in the [[Liga I]]. The club's current name combines the [[Hungarian language|Hungarian]] and [[Romanian language|Romanian names]] of the city, with [[Székelys]] representing the predominant ethnic group of Miercurea Ciuc. Originally established in 1904 in [[Austria-Hungary]] and refounded in 1919 in Romania, Csíkszereda competed in both the Romanian and Hungarian league systems during the first half of the 20th century, reaching the [[Nemzeti Bajnokság II|second tier]] of Hungarian football after [[Northern Transylvania]] was ceded to Hungary in 1940. Following [[World War II]], the club spent most of its history in the lower divisions of Romanian football, first reaching the [[Liga III|third tier]] in 1971. After the [[Romanian Revolution|fall of communism]] in 1989, financial difficulties led to periods of decline, including a withdrawal from competitions in 2000. Following its 2010 refoundation however, Csíkszereda climbed steadily through the league system, earning promotion to the [[Liga II|second division]] in [[2019–20 Liga II|2019]] and making its [[Liga I]] debut in the [[2025–26 Liga I|2025–26 season]]. The team plays its home matches at the [[Stadionul Municipal (Miercurea Ciuc)|Municipal Stadium]], which was redeveloped and expanded in the 2010s."}}
